Per-device VRAM at generation = GPU0 2096 MiB + GPU1 1502 MiB = 3598 MiB pool (3.773 decimal GB). Peak per device = 2096 MiB = 2.198 decimal GB.
Layer split is 58.3/41.7, NOT 50/50; a sizing rule must use peak-per-device, not total/2. The pool is 0.535 decimal GB above the single-GPU M1 reading (a second runtime context).

Measured on NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF, llama.cpp --cpu-moe, ctx 1024, concurrency 1.
Model: Qwen-Agentworld-35B-A3B, Q4_K_M (file 22.314 decimal GB, arch qwen35moe, HYBRID SSM+MoE, 256 experts top-8, full_attention_interval 4).

Resident GPU VRAM at generation = 3004 MiB = 3.150 decimal GB. Routed+shared experts (19.770 decimal GB) are offloaded to host RAM; observed host RAM delta ~8.4 decimal GB (mmap/page-cache, NOT a resident copy and NOT a prediction).

The MoE is a hybrid SSM+MoE: only 1 of 4 blocks is full attention, so per-token KV grows ~4x slower than a dense model at equal depth. This is why a 22.314 decimal GB model is resident in 3.150 decimal GB of VRAM.
Latency cost of offload: TTFT 1.737 s, ITL 0.1252 s, 7.3 tokens/s (vs 28.4 tokens/s for the dense 4B).
